title: Suppression of Extrinsic Anomalous Hall Conductivity in Disordered Parity Anomalous Semimetal
authors: Shi-Hao Bi, Bo Fu, Shun-Qing Shen
abstract: We present an analytical investigation of the extrinsic contributions to the anomalous Hall conductivity in the context of the half-quantized Hall effect observed in disordered parity anomalous semimetal emerged from semi-magnetic topological insulator thin films. The gapless Dirac cone surface state, which embodies the quintessence of the half-quantized Hall effect, exhibits remarkable robustness against disorder scattering. Two primary extrinsic mechanisms, the side-jump and skew-scattering, are deemed irrelevant and make no contributions. These results establish the parity anomalous semimetal as a disorder-resilient quantum phase, thereby providing insights into Dirac fermion physics.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes a Parity Anomalous Semimetal exhibiting a half-quantized Hall effect. By calculating the contributions from standard disorder mechanisms like side-jump and skew-scattering using advanced many-body techniques, the authors prove that these extrinsic effects vanish. This confirms the intrinsic robustness of the half-quantized topological state against realistic material disorder.
main_problem: The study investigates how extrinsic disorder contributions, specifically side-jump and skew-scattering mechanisms, affect the half-quantized anomalous Hall conductivity in a Parity Anomalous Semimetal (PAS).
main_result: The analysis rigorously demonstrates that both the side-jump and skew-scattering mechanisms make no net contribution to the half-quantized Hall conductance. This proves that the PAS phase is robust against such extrinsic disorder effects.
method: The investigation employs analytical techniques, including the self-consistent Born approximation (SCBA) within the Kubo formalism, applied to a tight-binding Hamiltonian model.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a disordered Parity Anomalous Semimetal (PAS), derived from semi-magnetic topological insulator thin films exhibiting gapless Dirac cone surface states. The analysis uses lattice Hamiltonians and incorporates on-site random potentials for disorder scattering.
key_observables: Anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), specifically its half-quantized value ($ rac{1}{2} e^2/h$), and the contributions from side-jump ($\sigma_{sj}$) and skew-scattering ($\sigma_{sk}$).
important_parameters: The Fermi level position relative to the Dirac cone, disorder strength ($W$), and scattering times ($	au$).
main_assumptions: Key assumptions include treating different scattering mechanisms as statistically independent and utilizing approximations like the Ioffe-Regel condition in certain regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate Feynman diagrams detailing various scattering contributions to $\sigma_{xy}$ and show schematic representations of how disorder affects gapless versus gapped Dirac cone states.
paper_structure: The paper follows a theoretical derivation, first establishing the model Hamiltonian and then systematically calculating the total anomalous Hall conductivity by evaluating the individual contributions from side-jump and skew-scattering terms using advanced Green's function techniques.
why_interesting: While focused on topological materials, the rigorous mathematical treatment of disorder effects (using SCBA) and the demonstration of robustness against scattering are highly relevant to understanding localization phenomena in complex quantum systems, which shares methodological overlap with disordered lattice models used in condensed matter theory.
